## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The bullet-prefix hint change is accurate. The rewritten criterion hint is not: it tells users to leave out "shall", but the `require_shall` option this PR says it keeps rejects any criterion without that word. The PR also adds `review.txt` at the repository root. The description doesn't mention it, it has no effect on the code, and it doesn't look like it belongs in this change.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — `CRITERION_HINT` now reads "Write criteria as direct action bullets without the word shall." But when `require_shall=True` (an option the PR body says it keeps, exposed as `require_shall` in `config.example.yml:1`), `accepts_criterion` returns `" shall " in text` (`app/criteria.py:7-8`). So `"- Save the result"`, which follows the hint exactly, is rejected. `tests/test_criteria.py:20-21` already asserts this rejection. Could the hint depend on the option, e.g. a separate hint for `require_shall=True` that asks for "shall", or could the "without the word shall" clause be dropped? — Anyone running with `require_shall: true` who follows the hint has every criterion rejected, and the hint gives them no way to fix it.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `BULLET_HINT` (`app/criteria.py:12`) now gives the exact `- ` prefix, which matches the `text.startswith("- ")` check at `app/criteria.py:5`.
